sourceConcerns.title: Publisher replay/rollback history can move with a peer alias
sourceConcerns.mechanism: The history bucket is current admitted peerId, or key-prefix only when no safe peer is found. Adding a peer for an already trust-list-admitted key or adding a lexically earlier alias for the same key changes the bucket scanned. A previously imported manifest may then be accepted again despite the same signing publisher.
sourceConcerns.nextWitness: Use existing operatorTrustHome and genuine export: import under key-derived bucket, add a peer for that same key, replay the exact package and require refusal with old state unchanged. Then use a distinct older package to test rollback across the alias transition.

sourceConcerns.classification: Source-derived adjacent containment concern; not reproduced here
sourceConcerns.title: Destination containment is lexical and does not admit existing parent links
sourceConcerns.mechanism: containedPath checks resolved path spelling. Staging directory creation and writes can follow a preexisting inbox or admitted-publisher parent symlink. Safe tar extraction addresses archive members, not these destination parents.
sourceConcerns.nextWitness: First prove a genuine regular import, then plant only a fixture-owned inbox/publisher directory link to a fixture-owned sibling and observe actual target effects. Retain any RED. Do not infer a symlink-free or atomic-race guarantee from current traversal tests.

sourceConcerns.classification: Atomicity and race scope limit; requires separate proof before stronger claim
sourceConcerns.title: Atomic inbox rename is not a transaction with benchmark ingestion
sourceConcerns.mechanism: The complete package is renamed into inbox before benchmark ingestion writes into another store. A filesystem failure there can leave a committed complete package and partial or absent benchmark state; replay may subsequently refuse retry. admitBenchmark does not reserve writable destination state.
sourceConcerns.nextWitness: A fixture-owned non-directory destination or another real IO refusal can clarify failure semantics without mocking producer/handler success. Existing requirement explicitly promises pre-trust checks and a complete inbox package, not a cross-store transaction.
